subject: Performance/SLO: Finwise load test coordination
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Performance/SLO: Finwise load test coordination

Hi Alex —

Great meeting earlier — thanks for walking through Finwise's expected traffic patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Recap of targets you mentioned:
- Target 95p latency for generation calls: <= 300ms (goal) / <= 500ms (SLO)
- Target throughput: sustained 500 req/s across the service (burst to 750 req/s for short windows)
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions
- Streaming: required (incremental token delivery for UI responsiveness)

What we need from Finwise for the load test:
1) Confirmation of a 2-hour test window (proposed: Tue Mar 3, 09:00–11:00 PT)
2) Production-like sample payloads (avg tokens in/out + typical system/system prompt sizes) — you indicated you can provide
3) IP allowlist for our test runners and the dedicated endpoint (we can provide ranges)
4) k6/Locust script — you mentioned you'd start from the k6 script we shared; we can host and iterate on it together

What Redwood will provide before the run:
- Test account/API key scoped to your environment (read-only metrics, throttles removed for the test)
- A candidate k6 script and a Drive link to the working copy (we'll push initial script by EOD today)
- IP ranges to add to your allowlist and a short checklist for network/NAT setup
- A monitoring dashboard showing token-level cost, 95/99 latency, error rates, and per-route throughput

Please confirm the proposed window and attach your sample payloads and any SRE requirements. Once confirmed we'll create the test API key and share the k6 script link.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: k6_finwise_script.js (stub)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finwise SRE <sre@finwise.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance/SLO: Finwise load test coordination

Thanks Logan — this looks good. Confirming details from our side: 

- Window: Tue Mar 3, 09:00–11:00 PT works for our SREs
- Payloads: I attached a small sample set (production-samples.zip) — typical request is ~1.2k tokens in, ~90 tokens out (generation).
- Streaming: required for our UX — we need chunked responses every ~150ms once tokens start streaming.
- Concurrency & throughput: Our goal is 200 concurrent streaming sessions, ramp to sustained 500 req/s. We will also run a couple short 5-minute bursts to 800 req/s to test headroom.

Action items on our side:
- We'll add Redwood IP ranges to our allowlist once you send them.
- We're happy to run the k6 script from the Drive link; our SRE will run from their nat'd ranges: 52.23.0.0/16 and 35.180.0.0/16 (example).

Would appreciate if Redwood can provide the test API key and a host-level endpoint (not behind additional WAF) so we can get accurate network latency. Also please add any required headers for session pinning/streaming.

Regards,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, Finwise
alex.johnson@finwise.com

--

Alex — thanks for confirming. Quick updates and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Test API key & endpoint:
- Created: finwise-loadtest-key-20260224 (we'll send the key via the secure portal link)
- Endpoint: https://finwise-loadtest.redwood.ai/v1/generate (this is a scoped test endpoint)

2) IP ranges for your allowlist (please add these to your firewall rules):
- 34.120.0.0/16
- 35.196.0.0/16
- 35.199.0.0/16
(we'll also add a short-lived NAT pool if you need a fixed egress for inbound callbacks)

3) k6 script & Drive link:
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/finwise/k6-script (we pushed k6_finwise_script.js and a README with ramp profiles)
- We tuned the script to simulate streaming by issuing chunked requests and validating chunk timing. Let us know if your team needs Locust instead — we can convert quickly.

4) Monitoring & success criteria:
- Redwood will monitor 95p latency, 99p latency, error rate (4xx/5xx) and token throughput.
- Success: 95p <= 500ms and error rate < 1% for sustained 500 req/s. If we see degradation we will automatically scale to backup model variant and notify SREs.

5) Test run plan (proposed):
- 09:00–09:15: ramp to 200 concurrent streaming sessions / 250 req/s
- 09:15–10:00: sustained 500 req/s (monitoring)
- 10:00–10:05: two 5-min bursts to 800 req/s
- 10:05–11:00: cooldown and follow-up exploratory runs as needed

Please confirm you have the sample payloads uploaded and that the proposed run plan works. Once you confirm I'll send the secure portal link with the API key and the attachment ip_allowlist_request.pdf which lists the same ranges and a checklist for your network team.

Thanks —

Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in operations/support — we will have a monitoring lead on the run and will watch the dashboard in real-time. A couple quick notes: 

- We'll track 95p and 99p latency, error rate, and per-route throughput. If 95p exceeds 500ms we'll trigger the canary fallback to the compatible model variant and alert your SREs.
- Please confirm expected tokens per request (Alex mentioned ~1.2k in / 90 out). That helps us size cache behavior and batch settings for the dedicated pool.
- If you need us to run the script from our runners as a cross-check we can do that, but we'd prefer your SREs run the canonical test from your nat ranges for accurate network numbers.

See you in the run — thanks!

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
